name: Dorsal hump rasping (DIY)

lead: Dorsal hump rasping refers to attempts to reduce a bump on the bridge of the nose without a surgeon, by filing or hitting it. Medical sources describe hump reduction as a step within rhinoplasty carried out by trained surgeons, and they do not describe a home method.
Because no published research or reliable source describes the DIY version, this entry is short.

paras: In surgery, the bony and cartilaginous bump on the nasal dorsum is reduced with instruments under anesthesia, after which the nose is typically splinted and taped [1]. Proponents of home methods have not published a mechanism in the sources reviewed.

Nasal bones and cartilage support breathing as well as shape, and after surgical rhinoplasty the nose is immobilised in a dressing and splint while it heals [1]. Injury, infection, airway and appearance problems are general concerns for any nasal trauma. No study evaluates the DIY practice.

lead: Dorsal hump rasping (DIY) is the name given to attempts to lower a bump on the nasal bridge at home by filing or striking it. The sources consulted for this wiki do not document how common the practice is or describe its methods.

In professional practice, reduction of a dorsal hump is part of rhinoplasty. After the surgeon reshapes the nose and closes incisions, the nose is dressed, taped and splinted to hold its position while it heals, and swelling can take at least a year to resolve fully [1].

paras: Rhinoplasty references describe surgeon-performed reshaping followed by taping and an external splint, with the dressing typically removed about a week after the operation [1]. Recovery involves prolonged swelling, and healing varies between individuals [1].
